{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Contractor Services Agreement (RadialSpark)

**To:** Deal team, Clear Capital (Company / Customer)
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Contract review findings and negotiation priorities

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. Eighteen rules were assessed: **eleven are compliant** and require no redline, **five are deviations**, and **two clauses the playbook expects are missing entirely**.

The commercial core is favourable to us. Ownership of the Works vests in Clear Capital with a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence back to Contractor's embedded pre-existing materials (§ 4), and the Agreement contains no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no liquidated damages, no auto-renewal and no audit right running against us. Engagement is task-by-task on time and materials under separately agreed Statements of Work.

The risk is concentrated in the risk-allocation and exit provisions:

- **No indemnity exists.** Section 7's heading promises indemnification but the section contains only liability caps and waivers; a full-text search for "indemnif" returns the heading alone. This is walk-away territory under our playbook.
- **The liability cap is broken.** Contractor's liability is capped at fees paid under the specific SOW, and the sole carve-out cross-refers to Paragraph 9 — the Independent Contractor clause — making the exception illusory. Confidentiality breaches and the non-infringement warranty currently sit inside the fee cap.
- **No cyber insurance**, despite Contractor handling Company data and accessing Company systems — also walk-away territory.
- **No exit from a live engagement.** The convenience right applies only when no SOW is outstanding, and there is no transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation at all.
- **No deliverable conformity warranty**, with the implied warranties disclaimed in § 5(e).
- **Arizona governing law** falls outside our accepted jurisdictions.

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Heading promises indemnity; no operative indemnity or hold-harmless anywhere. § 5(c) gives a bare non-infringement warranty with no defence obligation. Walk-away. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 7 | Per-SOW fees-paid cap below the mutual 12-month fallback; sole carve-out mis-refers to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), so no effective carve-outs for confidentiality, IP, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials; Acceptance | Works vest in Company with perfection assistance; perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence back. Minor: licence not stated "irrevocable"/"worldwide"; ownership attaches on invoice "paid" rather than paid or payable. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 10 (via § 7 finding ref) | Symmetrical consent with no affiliate/successor carve-out, so routine reorganisations and M&A need Contractor consent. No Contractor rights on our change of control (satisfactory). |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | Task-by-task SOW structure; no sole-source or requirements commitment. Preferred position met. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 6 Termination | On termination we pay only fees and expenses earned through the effective date; no kill fee, minimum fee or late-payment penalty. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 4(c) | Royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable; not revocable and not cut off by § 6. Sits at or above fallback. Minor: "irrevocable" not express; affiliates/contractors not named. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 4 / § 13 | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on Company. § 13 is a personnel restriction only (see item 11). |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 18 / § 19 (via § 7 finding ref) | Arizona law is outside the accepted list (NY, DE, CA, England and Wales); no venue clause, and arbitration confirmed in the losing party's district. Not walk-away (domestic seat). |
| 10 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 6 Termination | § 6(a) convenience right applies only when no SOW is outstanding; with an indefinite term we cannot exit a live engagement except for material breach. Fails the 60–90 day fallback. |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 13 | Mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel involved in the Services — but no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches, which the fallback treats as material. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 6 Termination | No transition assistance, no data or Confidential Information return, no deletion or certification. § 8 restricts use and disclosure but imposes no return duty. |
| 13 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5 Representations and Warranties; Disclaimer | No conformity warranty, no warranty period and no remedy; § 5(e) then disclaims implied warranties. Fails the 90-day fallback. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right runs against us; better than preferred. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 | No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation on us. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 3 / § 1(a) | Fees payable only for Services ordered and performed; no minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall charge. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 / § 2 / § 6(a) | No auto-renewal; term runs until terminated, with a 15-day convenience exit when no SOW is outstanding. Better than preferred. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 14 | Workers' comp, CGL USD 1M and E&O USD 1M (at fallback), but **no cyber/privacy cover of any amount** against a USD 2M fallback, while Contractor handles Company data and accesses our systems. Walk-away. |

## 3. Walk-away items

Two findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **Absence of any Vendor indemnity (item 1).** There is no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or wilful-misconduct indemnity in the document. We have inserted a Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d) with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics, carved out of the § 7(a) cap, together with a reciprocal Company indemnity narrowed to Company-furnished materials and Company's breach of law, and conformed the § 7 heading to remove the one-sided "OF CONTRACTOR".
2. **No cyber/privacy liability insurance (item 18).** "Confidential Information" in § 8 expressly captures Company data and records, and § 1 contemplates Contractor personnel working at our facilities and accessing our systems. We have added cyber/privacy cover at the preferred USD 5M, scoped to circumstances where Contractor handles Company data, and will offer the USD 2M fallback.

We also treat the **illusory liability carve-out (item 2)** as effectively non-negotiable: as drafted, a confidentiality or IP failure is capped at fees paid under a single SOW.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Send the redline** covering the five deviations and two missing clauses, in this order of priority: indemnity (§ 7(d)); liability cap and Excluded Claims; cyber insurance; termination for convenience and transition assistance; deliverable warranty; governing law and venue; assignment; non-solicitation carve-out.
2. **Liability cap position (item 2):** Contractor cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual defined set of uncapped Excluded Claims replacing the broken Paragraph 9 cross-reference, and confirmation that our fee obligations are not capped damages. The Company-side cap at fees paid is favourable to us and we leave it untouched.
3. **Exit package (items 10 and 12):** a 30-day Company convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW, payment only for Services performed plus refund of prepaid fees, no termination fee, and confirmation that Contractor has no convenience right while an SOW is outstanding; plus new § 6(c) transition assistance, data return and certified deletion, with the 90-day assistance window offered as the fallback. The mutual 15-day right in § 6(a) stays as drafted.
4. **Warranty (item 13):** insert a 90-day deliverable conformity warranty with repair, replace or refund remedy and a no-malicious-code assurance ahead of the § 5(e) disclaimer, which otherwise remains as drafted since it preserves express warranties.
5. **Governing law (item 9):** move to New York with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County and seat any arbitration in New York County; Delaware, California, or England and Wales with London courts are acceptable fallbacks.
6. **Assignment (item 4):** add the affiliate/successor carve-out on notice, bar Contractor assignment to a competitor of ours, and confirm a Company change of control is not a deemed assignment, retaining the mutual consent standard.
7. **Non-solicitation (item 11):** add the general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs only; we are not pressing deletion or the measurement date, given the clause is mutual and narrowly scoped.
8. **Watch items for the SOW template and any reopened sections.** Statements of Work sit outside this document, so any minimum hours or retainer floor proposed in an SOW should be reviewed under MINCOMMIT (§ 1(a) helpfully gives this Agreement priority over conflicting SOW terms), and any records-inspection right under AUDIT. Separately, § 3(b) permits Contractor to change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap; that is a pricing point for the pricing reviewer, mitigated by per-SOW fixed rates and the 15-day exit. If § 4 or § 14 is reopened, we would add "irrevocable", "worldwide", named affiliates and contractors, "paid or payable", a CGL aggregate, E&O at USD 2M and one-year tail coverage as clean-up."}
